Xernona Clayton discovered the document in her late husband Edward T. Clayton's desk, where it remained untouched for decades after his 1966 death. Clayton, who worked as a public relations director at the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, recently decided to auction it.

Scholar Drew D. Hansen highlighted King's careful word choices, noting he replaced "tokenism" and "waitism" with "gradualism" when warning of the "tranquilising drug of gradualism." Hansen said the document gave him "actual chills."

Christie's expects the sale to fetch over $10 million, with proceeds supporting the King Center in Atlanta and other philanthropic efforts chosen by Clayton. The document will travel to Chicago and New York after its Atlanta display.

The manuscript will be displayed at the National Center for Civil and Human Rights in Atlanta starting November 16, followed by exhibitions in Chicago and New York before the January auction. This marks the first public viewing of the historic draft.

China is unlikely to prop up prices, with "persistent weakness" in road-fuel usage set to scar demand by 400,000 barrels a day, according to Goldman analysts, as they estimate China's total oil demand peaked in 2025.

The US-Iran war initially choked regional production before suppliers tapped alternative export routes; production in the Middle East now rises via ship-to-ship transfers and new pipelines, contributing to downward price pressure.

Brent traded below $95 a barrel on Monday after dropping more than 1%, while The Paris-based International Energy Agency reported last Friday that the global oil market is swinging to a surplus for the first time since the conflict began.

Analysts expect a 2027 contest between high supply disruption risk and increasing market adaptation, with Brent futures averaging $88 a barrel next year and easing to $78 by year-end "as the risk premium gradually normalizes.
title: Goldman Sachs Warns of Massive Oil Glut in 2027

summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is expected to announce the disbanding of the New York Police Department's Strategic Response Group, potentially through an executive order, according to Politico.

Mamdani pledged to dissolve the SRG during his mayoral campaign last year, citing high rates of misconduct claims against the unit and arguing that counterterrorism and protest response should function separately.
The administration plans to replace the SRG with a civilian unit focused on deescalation, with NYPD officers assembling nearby to provide support and conduct arrests if needed, according to sources.

Sources suggest the announcement could come as early as Friday, potentially preceding a Saturday convention held by the New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists, which has prioritized disbanding the SRG.

NYPD brass has defended the SRG as highly trained experts in counterterrorism and crowd control, though the administration maintains that separating protest response from counterterrorism remains a core goal.

summary: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop due to communications issues, resulting in over 3,220 cancellations and roughly 10,200 delays across the United States.
Officials are investigating whether the FAA's new $875 million Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories system played a role, following its rollout to 22 centers on Nov. 10.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters the disruption was a "telecommunications outage," not a national security threat, stating, "You can't rule out anything at this point."
Air Space Intelligence stated on X that the ground stop is "not based on or a result of the SMART system," while Microsoft confirmed "no indication" of a link to its services.
This incident marks only the third nationwide ground stop in U.S. history. Mullin emphasized "there is no reason for the public to be afraid" regarding safety concerns.

The US-led Pax Silica initiative, formed in December 2025, aims to secure supply chains for silicon and critical minerals essential to advanced technologies, addressing concerns about Beijing's rapid progress.

Participants affirmed that economic security is fundamental to national security, identifying critical infrastructure underpinning Super Intelligence supply chains as a priority for coalition members.
The San Francisco Declaration resolves to establish five working groups to carry common purpose into practice, including frameworks for Super Intelligence adoption and security resilience.
Coalition members stated that no nation can secure the foundations of the Super Intelligence era alone, cementing shared principles into a working partnership to ensure durable infrastructure.
title: US, 9 partners sign agreement to secure AI supply chains

Israel's Channel reported Sunday that Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden allegedly directed police to a purported intelligence source, leading to the wrongful arrest of three Raam members who were later released.

Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main rival and former army chief of staff, stated the caretaker prime minister 'cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer,' while Yair Lapid of the Beyachad list called the events an 'attempted coup.'

Raam's Yoav Segalovitz, a former police chief, demanded an 'immediate, independent and thorough criminal investigation' into those involved, asserting Netanyahu 'tried to steal the country' after claiming his own election was being stolen.

Neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Eisenkot's opposition secured the 61 seats needed to form a government following the October election, while His Likud party denied the allegations and Haaretz reported Shin Bet chief David Zini previously sought to wiretap the Joint List.

summary: On Sunday, Somaliland's National Intelligence Agency briefly detained five Americans citing national security concerns; the group departed on an Ethiopian Airlines flight Monday.

Foreign Affairs Minister Abdirahman Dahir Adam invited the group to conduct investment feasibility studies on November 4, while the five work for Parallel Black, registered in Delaware less than two months ago.
The NIA claimed it conducted a "lengthy investigation" into the Americans' activities, yet provided no details regarding their identities or alleged actions in the Horn territory.
Somaliland, which declared independence from Somalia in 1991, occupies a strategic location at the juncture of the Indian Ocean and Red Sea, heightening security sensitivities.

Israel recognized Somaliland as a sovereign state last December, prompting lobbying for United States recognition; NIA Director-General Jama Mohamoud Egal and the State Department did not respond to requests for comment.
title: Somaliland briefly detains Americans accused of threatening national security

summary: On Sunday, Attorney Aaron Reitz of the Southern District of Texas demanded that Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren preserve records connected to prospective investigations of people associated with President Donald Trump, citing two federal civil-rights statutes, 18 USC 241 and 242.

Reitz had already issued public warnings last week to Democratic Senators Richard Blumenthal and Elissa Slotkin under Title 18. He cited Warren's remarks on CBS Face The Nation signaling intent to "target private individuals close to President Trump."

Warren responded, "We have to do both. If you've been making your profits by cheating American families and scamming your investors, you better get ready for some investigations." She argued Americans are tired of a White House that failed to enforce laws.

White House chief of staff Stephen Miller responded on X by reposting Reitz's letter with "18 USC 241 and 242." Lawmakers who fail to comply with preservation requests could face sanctions, penalties, or other legal consequences.

Warren has until November 23 to confirm compliance with the preservation request. Incoming House Oversight Committee chair Garcia stated, "We're not going to be deterred, and we're certainly not going to be intimidated by Donald Trump or anyone in the administration.
title: DOJ warns Senator Warren about potential Trump-related probes

summary: Sixteen Ecuadorian fishers are suing the American government in District Court on Monday, alleging forces abducted and tortured them after a March 17 drone strike sank their boat, the Negra Francisca Duarte.

The lawsuit targets Operation Southern Spear, an administration boat-strike campaign launched in late 2025, which the Washington Office estimates has killed at least 238 people while officials provide scant evidence of narcotics trafficking.

Two armed drones destroyed the vessel 385 nautical miles from Manta, Ecuador , on March 17, severely burning two crew members, despite prior Ecuadorian authorities' inspections confirming the boat carried no drugs.

Survivors claim uniformed personnel hooded and jailed them for weeks in El Salvador; Dan Kovalik, the attorney representing the fishermen, says the men seek accountability from the incoming Democrat-controlled Congress for the "manifestly unlawful" attacks.

This filing joins mounting legal challenges, including a wrongful death lawsuit from Trinidadian fishers and an ACLU Freedom of Information Act suit demanding release of secret Justice Department legal opinions justifying the strikes.
title: 16 Ecuadorian Fishermen File Lawsuit Against Trump Administration Over U.S. Military Strike and Detention

summary: On Monday, November 16, 2026, the Institute of International Education reported a 9% decline in overall international student enrollment at U.S. universities this fall, with new foreign student enrollment plummeting 15%.

Changing visa policies under the Trump administration and growing global competition have fueled these declines; 88% of institutions identify the visa application process as a major factor, while 70% cite travel restrictions.

Despite overall enrollment declines, participation in the Optional Practical Training program rose 14.1% to 335,785 last year; the Department of Homeland Security proposed $70,000 fees per OPT student.

International students contribute nearly $40 billion annually to the U.S. economy, yet NAFSA reported a $2.4 billion decline in economic contributions this autumn, straining university budgets nationwide.

Early indicators suggest the international enrollment pipeline is weakening, with 95% of schools predicting students will consider other countries if OPT opportunities are restricted, pointing to further losses ahead.
title: Fewer Students Are Traveling From Abroad to Study at US Universities, Report Shows

summary: On Wednesday, November 11, 2026, NDLEA operatives arrested Chinedu Onwude at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos after discovering 25.05kg of methamphetamine concealed inside cereal packs in his checked luggage.

Onwude, who holds Nigerian and South African passports, admitted during interrogation he had lived in South Africa for over 24 years using a stolen identity and was contracted by a South Africa-based contact to deliver the drugs for 20,000 South African rands.

In Kaduna State on Monday, November 9, NDLEA operatives raided an alleged illegal firearms manufacturing factory, recovering 17 locally made Dane guns, two pistols, and 25 Dane gun pipes from the facility.

Saturday's joint operation in Ajah recovered 78.8kg of cannabis from an abandoned vehicle, while Delta State operatives arrested a 43-year-old woman with 255.67kg of cannabis sativa on Thursday, November 12.

summary: On November 13, shareholders filed a class action lawsuit in San Jose, California, against Intel , Chief Executive Tan Lip-Bu, and Chief Financial Officer David Zinsner, alleging the company defrauded investors by concealing a prolonged personal computer sales slowdown.
Raising capital in mid-August, Intel sold US$23 billion of stock at US$95 per share before shares plunged 28.6% on October 30, wiping out about US$140 billion of market value.

The lawsuit alleges Intel made "materially false and/or misleading" statements as "depressed demand for PC sales" caused a 9% drop in quarterly earnings to US$8.1bn, contradicting earlier claims demand was improving.
Intel shares closed at US$59.66 on November 13 following the legal action; the company did not immediately respond to requests for comment as of November 15.

Chief Executive Tan previously told analysts the industry faced an "unprecedented memory crunch" and manufacturing shortages, while problems with PC inventory and sales outweighed benefits from data center investments.
title: Investors sue chip giant Intel after 29% stock plunge

summary: A rare Georgia Keeffe painting discovered in a Manhattan closet after decades of storage is now on display at Christie's, valued between $3 million and $5 million before Tuesday's auction.
After purchasing the Keeffe painting for $3,800 in 1963, the owner kept it hidden in her closet until around 2022, when she casually mentioned it to her niece during a conversation.

Tylee Abbott, director of American Art at Christie's, called the Lobo Peak painting "particularly important because of its early date and its representation of the inception point of O'Keeffe's time in the American Southwest."
Experts believe the 1930 work is the first of three paintings in a series; one resides in the Metropolitan Museum, while the Rockefeller family held the other for many years.
Family members who requested anonymity discovered the treasure while cleaning the late owner's apartment this year; she had worked with the Foreign Service and lived into her 90s.
title: A Georgia O'Keeffe Painting Was Buried in a New York Apartment Closet. It Is Going up for Auction
